originality.rationale: The original same-object Schrijver result is chromatic and criticality, Matousek–Ziegler supplies topological chromatic bounds, Grohe–Otto supplies abstract pebble games. Their inspected claims do not imply this sharp local-extension theorem or the all-depth 3-variable consequence. A finite search is not a novelty certificate; residual historical risks are explicit.
residual_risks: An undiscovered general theorem on two-existential closure of stable Kneser graphs, graph disjointness systems, or induced stable-subset graphs could cover the threshold despite no matching retrieved statement; same-family sources on coloring, homomorphism spaces and shifts were inspected.
The original 1978 source establishes an earlier public year but no exact day could be independently verified. Date 2002-08-09 is the earliest exact-day public source used.
Literature and available research-record retrieval have limited recall; negative search alone cannot establish uniqueness or worldwide priority.

value.rationale: The first sharp all-parameter answer to a natural four-pattern local extension invariant of the classical vertex-critical Schrijver family, equating it to every-edge-triangle geometry. The induced permanent FO3 indistinguishability from the random graph persists through an unbounded chromatic spectrum, which is a motivated logical expressive-power boundary rather than routine finite enumeration.
